summary_rationale: NBIL (GraniteShares 2x Long NBIS Daily ETF) fails fundamental compounding standards on two independent layers. First, as a 1940 Act daily-reset single-stock ETF (1.41% net / 1.50% gross expense ratio, Total Return Swap financing spreads, and quadratic daily volatility decay), NBIL is mathematically engineered for single-day tactical exposure rather than multi-month compounding, evidenced by its -61.48% trailing 1-year return. Second, the underlying operating business, Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS), while scaling revenue rapidly ($529.8M FY2025; $980.8M Q3 2026) on >$40B–$46B of Microsoft and Meta backlog, remains deeply Free Cash Flow negative (-$3,664.1M in FY2025; ~$27B FY2026E CapEx; $40B–$45B FY2027E CapEx) and has transformed its balance sheet to $14.19B carrying debt ($16.48B principal) plus a $3.5B Citi credit facility, with narrow switching-cost moats and GPU obsolescence risk. Operational KPIs (backlog, >4 GW contracted power, Q3 2026 revenue) warrant PASS_WITH_WATCH due to CapEx escalation, colocation delays, and ARR-guidance retirement, but NBIL itself is structurally unsuitable as a long-term fundamental holding.
